# projr compatibility and change log

The [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) owns current product decisions. This log
records comparison evidence, implementation differences and gaps. Update it in
every focused PR; do not infer runtime parity from similar source or green Rust CI.

Relationship labels are **same**, **different**, **new**, and **unverified**.
Each entry states whether that label concerns documented intent, static source,
or executed behavior. No comparative R runtime tests have been run for the entries
below. Local R/Docker workloads have not been run.

## Reference baselines

- R baseline: [SATVILab/projr at 3ac2959](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/tree/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d).
- Thesis baseline: [design at b110da5](https://github.com/SATVILab/Manuscript22RodoThesis/blob/b110da557b802341e425f57f4acaa0c2b4ab97cb/projr/3-design.qmd).
- Rust pre-migration baseline: [024589b](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/tree/024589bbb6d471c3b1430057f76f5b2149444fac).

New comparisons must pin source commits and relevant files, record the decision
and rationale, link executed tests, and distinguish approved, implemented and
unverified behavior. Changing a reference baseline does not silently change the
product contract.

## PR123: development-preview mutation gates

- **Relationship: unverified runtime parity; same documented intent.** The R
  [README](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/README.md)
  and thesis design describe development previews separately from publication.
  This is evidence of intent, not proof that every R development path is inert.
- **Decision/rationale:** keep CLI-managed release/version/archive changes out of
  previews so researchers can inspect development results without publishing.
- **Implemented:** [PR123](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/123), merged
  `5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411`; Dev-gated VERSION writes, cleanup,
  document promotion, local export and ignore updates in
  [build.rs](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/blob/5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411/src/build.rs),
  env.rs and yml.rs.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform Rust tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39479251265),
  including `test_preview_safety.rs`, and installer checks passed on reviewed
  head `5d3ac227f52b33fd0c32fddd479cb7296c4072a5`. A disposable installed-CLI
  Python fixture reproduced the previous version/output/ignore mutations.
- **Gaps:** cooperating Python scripts only; renderer YAML rewriting, automatic
  output isolation, repeated runs, same-project concurrency and full production
  lifecycle behavior were not established. Subprocesses are not a sandbox.

## PR124: product authority and renderer contract

- **Relationship: new explicit contract; renderer parity unverified.** R
  [path.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/path.R)
  dynamically discovers a root, while the thesis defines the project workflow.
- **Decision/rationale:** current approved behavior supersedes defects and stale
  architecture claims. Root/path defaults must agree across projr,
  `quarto::quarto_render()` and RStudio QMD Render. Quarto root equals proj root;
  nested Quarto projects are unsupported. Direct rendering does not imply release
  lifecycle parity; R Markdown Knit is a separate entrypoint.
- **Implemented:** [PR124](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/124), merged
  `635aa9efac0d7a28971236ab78c879b21be5ec31`, corrected AGENTS/README/flow guidance
  and added the behavior contract. This was documentation, not renderer code.
- **Executed evidence:** independent document review and
  [remote Rust CI](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39481010442)
  passed at `dbf8d5fd94a87bba32ffc95cd2ee3b47f1e04277`.
- **Gaps:** no direct R frontend, Quarto/RStudio GUI or fresh-render-session
  parity test was performed. No projr production code or thesis text was changed.

## PR125: captured root and explicit selection

- **Relationship: different root-resolution mechanism; new CLI selection.** R
  [path.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/path.R)
  calls root discovery from current context. The CLI now captures one absolute
  root and passes it to each managed child as `PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT`.
- **Decision/rationale:** explicit selection wins, and path queries must not
  change projects after cwd changes. This deliberately improves unstable root
  behavior rather than copying it.
- **Implemented:** [PR125](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/125), merged
  `f265eb46c91a300fe0aafad3119d998038946a0b`; project.rs, ignore.rs, main.rs and
  build.rs. Direct library builds configure each child command instead of
  mutating the caller's process-global root.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39481104695)
  at `779b3010040eeb23f08434478e0812173eb2a723` cover explicit precedence, spaces,
  invalid roots, changed cwd and overlapping builds in two distinct roots.
- **Gaps:** marker discovery was not changed; R path helpers and direct render
  entrypoints do not yet consume this captured context. The tests do not promise
  general environment isolation or same-project concurrent builds.

## PR126: nonmutating queries and initializer failure preservation

- **Relationship: same static read-only configuration intent; runtime R parity
  unverified.** R [yml.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml.R)
  reads/merges configuration; this does not establish equivalence of every R
  public path helper or its cache routing.
- **Decision/rationale:** reading configuration or paths must not update ignore
  files. Mutating build/init operations request synchronization explicitly, and
  bad configuration must not replace custom ignores with default rules.
- **Implemented:** [PR126](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/126), merged
  `cd34c3208f1ed1c3c27571e7ce2828498a4aecdb`; yml.rs, build.rs, init.rs/main.rs.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39482261938)
  at `cc132f1e1b288c7560ff6b6b06fcac369a475355` snapshot files/directories for CLI
  queries, exercise direct API reads and production ignore synchronization, and
  preserve custom ignores on malformed/read-failing config. Permission-denied
  coverage ran on Linux/macOS.
- **Gaps:** supported aliases, unknown-option handling and effective merged
  script/hook configuration remained unchanged and incomplete.

## PR127: operation failures and exit status

- **Relationship: new CLI transport contract; same failure-reporting intent.** R
  [build-engine.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/build-engine.R)
  uses R errors; that is not a process exit-code protocol for language wrappers.
- **Decision/rationale:** a printed error must not be returned as successful
  execution. Failed Git remote inspection must not proceed to GitHub creation.
- **Implemented:** [PR127](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/127), merged
  `8e955b32bc1f611d38a8931d489de2bdfc50d5c7`; main.rs routes operation failures to
  nonzero status and init.rs propagates previously swallowed external failures.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39482993953)
  at `a741b5f9de63dcb96ca527607105e5547be1da7c` cover failing queries/version/init/
  ignores, missing executables, child failure and successful queries. Local fake
  Git/GitHub commands on Linux/macOS made no network requests.
- **Gaps:** structured error/capability protocols and clean/idempotent Git-init
  coverage remained open; failure status is not rollback or R-runtime parity.

## PR128: explicit noninteractive execution

- **Relationship: new CLI mode.** The R baseline's
  [build-engine.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/build-engine.R)
  calls dependency helpers; no equivalent explicit CLI flag/parity is claimed.
- **Decision/rationale:** machine invocations must not need the CLI's prompts or
  automatic package installation. Controlled child stdin must actually be closed.
- **Implemented:** [PR128](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/128), merged
  `f7ff7e92451a3174d6cb9c5fd60151621e66bd04` after independent review at
  `5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1`; adds the flag, inherited mode,
  runner stdin closure and controlled R-probe stdin closure.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39484182256)
  and installer checks passed at that head; fake-R EOF/no-install tests ran on
  Linux/macOS and Python runner-stdin coverage ran on all three platforms.
- **Gaps:** no actual R startup/renderer execution comparison; initialization
  retains existing requested-operation defaults and third-party code can ignore
  EOF. This does not establish general subprocess isolation.

## PR129: explicit empty selection and newly confirmed policies

- **Relationship: same absent-dev fallback; different explicit-empty guarantee.** R
  [yml-scripts.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml-scripts.R)
  falls back when dev scripts are absent. Empty-list behavior also passes through
  [validation](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml-check.R)
  and renderer selection, so a reliable R upload-only no-analysis contract has
  not been demonstrated.
- **Decision/rationale:** explicit `[]` selects no analysis, preserving hooks and
  production upload/export; absence still falls back. It must not discover or
  render unrequested files. Cleanup/promotion must preserve upload inputs.
- **Implementation status:** [PR129](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/129)
  removes the Dev-empty error and derives one analysis-selection guard for
  renderer setup/cleanup/promotion. `tests/test_empty_scripts.rs` checks hooks,
  existing output/docs bytes, actual production archive bytes and preview
  nonpublication.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform Rust tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39485258868)
  and [installer checks](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39485258718)
  passed at `f4b3739554dc548911019c450ca1e90a196d33d2`; independent review inspected
  those logs and cleared that code head. The documentation-only final head
  `999b730fd2cc23215e4a07a1231d7d6fa3543966` passed all nine checks in
  runs 39486028024/39486028097 and independent review. Merged as
  `5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb`; post-merge test, installer
  and site runs 39486858711/39486858532/39486858701 passed.
- **Gaps:** YAML null-as-absence and malformed-list validation were inspected in
  source, not newly exercised by this policy slice. No R runtime empty-list parity
  test or real renderer execution is claimed.
- **Confirmed but separate runtime gaps:** retain projr markers (including README/
  VERSION), accept legacy `_projr.yml` with a both-base-files error, and use local
  > profiles > base with earlier profiles first. The R precedence evidence is
  [yml.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml.R#L224).
  These approvals are recorded in the behavior contract; this change does not
  implement aliases, marker expansion or merged script/hook context.

## Ponytail source verification and completed-chunk review

The actual [.agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/blob/be625b670b914c85b669257eefd60ae678662d33/.agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md)
is vendored unchanged from DietrichGebert/ponytail **v4.10.0**, upstream commit
`e3ba2aa6f1e6f0bc4d69eb09c9f0d0a93af56156`, as installed by PR121. Its pinned
upstream bytes and the existing projcli, projr, setupmjr and projects copies all
have SHA-256 `1316a2f3f95741d2300b116fe0c2d81ce4a9568656ed0a62643f54aaf09957f2`.
The established setupmjr vendoring contract matches; no duplicate or replacement
skill was installed.

The skill prescribes the full-mode simplicity ladder, tracing callers before
changing shared behavior, reusing existing code/stdlib/dependencies, and leaving
an appropriate runnable check. It supplies no separate executable review script.
Applying that guidance is a self-review, separate from independent review and CI.

Completed-chunk review of PR128 at `5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1`:

- Traced the prompt helpers, main description prompt, dependency probes, install
  branch, script/hooks and project-render runners. Reused the existing EnvGuard,

  custom execution framework was introduced.
- Finding/action: the R package probe also needed closed stdin before package
  detection. That path was corrected and covered by a live-input/fake-R EOF test.
  Rechecking all controlled status/output paths found no further necessary change.
- All three remote Rust suites and installers passed; this self-review remained
  separate from the independent exact-head review.

Completed-chunk review of PR129's empty-selection change:

- Reused the existing explicit-list resolver and pipeline; no new execution
  framework, configuration key or dependency was added.
- Traced preflight, version, cleanup, hooks, document promotion and publication.
  Finding: skipping script execution alone could still erase upload-only inputs
  or require unused renderers. Action: derive one shared analysis-selection guard
  and apply it before those stages; keep hooks/publication outside that guard.
- Retained data-preservation and failure handling. Added runnable integration
  checks for real archive bytes and absence-versus-empty semantics; those checks

  runtime parity was inferred.

## Nearest recognized roots (current change)

- **Relationship: same static projr marker intent; deliberate extensions.**
  [projr path.R at 3ac2959](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/path.R#L277)
  combines VCS, VERSION, README, R-package, RStudio, renv and Quarto criteria.
  Exact structured-marker patterns were checked in
  [rprojroot root.R at 4d2f450](https://github.com/r-lib/rprojroot/blob/4d2f450c3f67b98a3599fe8531bdda1c4c928cc1/R/root.R).
- **Decision/rationale:** retain those markers with nearest-wins; remove Rust's
  VERSION-first/five-extra-ancestors heuristic. Add pyproject.toml and Julia
  Project.toml/JuliaProject.toml as requested language extensions. Proj config
  files also anchor a configured project without VERSION. Requirements/orphan
  manifests do not create roots. Explicit selection still wins.
- **Implementation/evidence status:** `root_from` now tests each ancestor once,
  never child projects. `tests/test_root_markers.rs` covers retained marker
  patterns, invalid structured markers, weak/nested markers, deep invocation,
  explicit override and a configured Python preview with shallow enumeration.
  At code head `a0d459c5b3a31437443832436535b70d34838553`, all nine checks
  passed in runs 39487247962/39487247928. Independent review compared the pinned
  marker sources and inspected all three platform logs, clearing that head.
  Symlink normalization was source-inspected, without a new dedicated test.
  Final evidence-only head `55e5606e7916f78de7dfb03a4bb43b0ae1a87987`
  passed all nine checks in runs 39487685152/39487685131 and independent review;
  merged as `41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1`. No R-runtime parity is claimed.
- **Gaps:** required active config, explicit used-directory mappings, early
  unsupported-setting validation, legacy config-content aliases and full
  frontend/renderer parity are separate changes. A marker does not claim a Julia runner exists.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** reused the public root_from entrypoint, existing
  regex dependency and standard filesystem APIs, replacing the old special-case
  traversal instead of adding a discovery framework. Traced explicit/inherited
  precedence and all root callers. Kept discovery read-only and shallow, with
  runnable positive/negative predicates and workflow coverage; no new dependency.

## Superseding configuration, failure and R-scope decisions

- **Relationship: different from prior convenience-default assumptions.** The
  initial Rust/projr-style defaults and historical no-config fixtures are no
  longer the target behavior. Builds require active root-level configuration and
  explicit used-directory mappings; init may write familiar defaults into that
  file, but runtime must not invent missing directories or unknown subpaths.
- **Decision status:** approved. The agreed `_proj.yml` / legacy `_projr.yml`
  names apply; explicitly activated profile files may provide configuration,
  while inactive profiles alone do not satisfy the requirement. Cwd discovery
  fallback does not waive build validation. Unknown behavior-affecting settings
  must fail before mutation.
- **Failure/publication target:** restore pre-build state except permitted cache
  residue; storage/publication retry must not rerun or mislabel analysis. Existing
  staging/version/publication behavior does not yet prove that transaction.
- **Evidence/gaps:** earlier CI entries remain accurate historical evidence for
  their source commits, not acceptance of the superseded no-config/default-path
  policy. Future fixtures must declare used paths and active configuration.
  The current core still needs enforcement and failure tests for the new rules.
- **Authorship boundary:** the existing R package is entirely off limits, including
  root-helper fixes. A later backend port/integration must establish R parity;
  no such work or runtime comparison is claimed here. Thesis text remains untouched.


## Base aliases and profile precedence (current change)

- **Relationship:** same projr local > profiles > base precedence, with
  earlier-listed profiles winning; legacy `_projr.yml` is accepted alongside
  canonical `_proj.yml` as an explicit compatibility decision. Both base files
  together fail instead of silently merging. Source comparison remains
  [projr yml.R at 3ac2959](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml.R#L224).
- **Implemented:** shared base selection for merged reads, existing build base
  inspection, parameters insertion and local-profile cloning. Explicit profile
  lists replace ambient lists; traversal-like explicit names fail validation.
  Profile/local files retain their existing `_projr-` names in this bounded slice.
- **Evidence:** new runnable query/alias/ambiguity/preservation/precedence tests
  passed on all three platforms at `53463d325c85c538ae0b8a5e792caa6bc997e452`.
  All nine checks in runs 39488461110/39488461213 passed; independent review
  inspected alias, precedence and duplicate-key logs and cleared that head.
  Final documentation/instruction head `c8b208f9243f828de05977f8e76d6f2074535a9b`
  passed all nine checks in runs 39489639669/39489639654 and independent review;
  merged as `0fec2735355ee5e9b9ba64d33ecd4796bf396301`. Post-merge checks passed.
  No R runtime tests.
- **Gaps:** one merged build script/hook context, active-configuration requirement,
  explicit directory mappings and early unsupported-setting validation remain
  separate work. This does not claim builds yet satisfy those approved rules.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** traced base filename readers and reused one
  stdlib path selector; reversed existing deep-merge traversal rather than adding
  a merger or dependency. Preserved null-as-absence and explicit-empty-list
  behavior. Checks exercise real query results and preservation on ambiguity.


PR131 failure-path review found that direct YAML-to-JSON deserialization allowed
duplicate keys to overwrite earlier values. Restored YAML Value parsing before
JSON conversion, preserving duplicate-key rejection at every active layer.
Added top-level and nested duplicate-key regressions for both base filenames,
profile and local files, including CLI failure before preview state writes.
The prior green CI did not cover this malformed-input case; the corrected head
above passed the new checks and independent re-review. Ponytail review kept this at the
shared file parser rather than guarding individual callers.

## Future R wrapper distribution boundary

- **Relationship: new/unverified design.** The
  [durable CRAN note](r-wrapper-cran.qmd) records the discussed future R-code wrapper
  around a separately installed CLI, meaningful unconditional R-only/mocked tests,
  conditional executable integration on CRAN, and mandatory pinned/checksummed CLI
  integration in our own CI. It cites current policy and pinned Quarto precedent.
- No existing R code or tests were changed; no CRAN submission, agreement,
  preinstalled executable, automatic-download exemption or renderer parity is
  claimed. Implementation and runtime validation remain future work.
- **Ponytail full-mode design review:** kept one linked design note; reused the
  repository's behavior/compatibility/AGENTS pointers. No installer, wrapper,

## One merged build script/hook context (current change)

- **Relationship:** follows projr's merged-configuration intent and the approved
  local > earlier profiles > later profiles > base precedence. The prior Rust
  pipeline validated merged settings but separately reread the base for execution.
- **Implemented:** deserialize and validate one merged value, then select scripts
  and hooks from it. Explicit empty dev selection remains empty; absence falls
  back to build settings. Both base filenames use this same execution path.
  Configuration parsing/validation, target resolution and preflight now precede
  production environment-ignore writes.
- **Evidence:** runnable Python fixtures check conflicting profiles, legacy base,
  local dev overrides and hook results, plus invalid merged configuration with a
  local environment file and missing-target failures leaving ignores/version/cache untouched. Remote CI and
  independent review pending; no real R/renderer execution is claimed.
- **Gaps:** required active config, explicit mappings, all unsupported-field
  rejection and transactional rollback remain separate approved work. Environment
  loading still uses the existing process-global guard; this change makes no new
  same-process concurrent environment guarantee.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** removed the second base-only YAML parser and its
  ignored parse failure instead of adding a second configuration model. Reused
  existing typed validation and dev fallback rules. Traced validation, selection,
  hooks and environment-ignore writes; retained explicit error propagation.


## Legacy audit tracking

The [2026-10-20 static audit](legacy-audit-20261020.qmd) records the pinned baseline,
reported failure paths, required regressions and correction order. Its findings
are not runtime reproductions or completed fixes. Highest managed-state risks
remain blockers to production-safety claims; arbitrary external script effects
are outside managed rollback. No mechanical edition upgrade or CAS redesign is
claimed. This review uses the actual Ponytail full-mode skill to prioritize root
causes and data-preservation checks over cosmetic rewriting.

## Active configuration and unsupported fields (prepared change)

- **Relationship: deliberate difference** from projr convenience defaults, as
  explicitly approved. Every build requires a base file or activated profile;
  inactive profile/local files alone do not qualify. Discovery still falls back
  to cwd independently. Empty analysis is valid with active configuration.
- **Implemented:** build gate before writes; unsupported typed configuration
  fields fail instead of disappearing in a top-level filter. Build failures
  include their error causes so unsupported-field diagnostics name the field. Arbitrary parameter
  and metadata maps remain supported and parameter aliases reach validation.
- **Evidence:** runnable tests cover active/base/legacy/inactive/local/no-config
  cases, unsupported nested keys, dynamic maps and no pre-build state writes.
  Remote CI/independent review pending. Explicit directory enforcement is still
  a separate gap; this does not yet establish transaction/promotion safety.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** reused Serde's unknown-field validation and the
  existing active profile resolver; removed silent filtering from runtime reads.
  No new parser/schema/dependency. Kept the old public filter helper only for
  compatibility; runtime no longer uses it.

PR135 review found mixed parameter aliases survived per-file parsing as separate
keys and then conflicted at typed deserialization. Canonicalize the one accepted
alias to `parameters` in the shared reader before merging. New fixtures cover all
64 base/profile/local alias combinations, earlier-profile precedence and retained
nested values; same-file multiple aliases and YAML duplicate keys remain errors.
Ponytail full-mode re-review kept the fix at the shared loader, without caller
guards or a second merge model. Exact amended CI/re-review remain required.

## Destructive destination guards (prepared change)

- **Relationship: new safety checks**, not a blanket ban on external resources.
  Before production analysis cleanup, reject root/ancestor destinations, staging
  and resource overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, label path
  separators and symlinked managed-write paths. Directory replacement also
  requires an existing source and disjoint destination before deleting bytes.
- **Evidence:** runnable preservation fixtures cover root, ancestor, staging,
  raw/output overlaps, traversal labels, Unix symlink parents and low-level
  self/ancestor/nested/missing-source moves. Remote CI/review pending.
- **Limits:** does not yet provide atomic promotion or complete rollback, protect
  against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement, undo user-script external
  effects or establish full CAS integrity. External disjoint paths remain valid.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** one stdlib identity resolver shared by build and
  promotion guards; trace all promotion callers, retain explicit errors instead
  of silently accepting missing source/read errors. No new dependency.


Path-guard Ponytail re-review traced the public cleanup helpers as well as build:
direct clear_pre/clear_post now apply the shared destination checks, clear_old
rejects symlinked staging parents, and traversal-bearing version components fail
before cache deletion. Label separator validation lives in shared typed validation
for all modes. Generic destructive move APIs require resolved parents and reject
symlink aliases; positive direct-API fixtures canonicalize their temporary roots
so macOS system temp aliases do not violate that explicit safety precondition.
Added a direct-cleanup preservation fixture. This is not complete transactional
restoration or a guarantee against concurrent filesystem replacement.

PR137 independent review found that configured-root checks alone missed derived
version/output cache leaves. Validate all actual cleanup bases before the first
deletion, including configured-cache and legacy staging paths. Direct dev cleanup
is now a true no-op. The same review traced individual document promotion and
recursive copying: validate paths before creating directories or renaming files,
require actual outputs, reject traversal/aliasing and prevalidate asset moves.
The two duplicate individual-renderer helpers now reuse one guarded implementation.
Added targeted direct-API regressions; amended remote CI/re-review are required.
This does not yet fix build callers discarding promotion errors or provide full
restoration/atomicity; those remain the following focused work.


The repaired PR137 guard prevalidates concrete generated-file/asset paths and both
legacy/configured cache-derived leaves before VERSION/ignore writes, including
dangling links. Individual and project promotion now resolve the configured docs
destination rather than a root/docs fallback; Python-only builds do not clear
unrelated docs. Unix fake-Quarto/fake-R CLI fixtures exercise the reported linked
root/docs sentinel bypass and actual successful external promotion, without a real

Project-render source safety is explicitly conservative: recognized source-like
`.qmd`, `.Rmd`, `.md` and `.ipynb` files or links in managed cleanup trees cause an
early error. This can reject generated Markdown there; it is not exact Quarto or
Bookdown input discovery. Keep sources and managed destinations separate until a
renderer-provided input plan is supported. Quarto's documented project input types
are described in [Project Basics](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/quarto-projects.html#render-targets).


The prepared literal-root glob fix is included in PR137 because a metacharacter
root otherwise hides explicit inputs from the cleanup containment guard. Reuse
glob::Pattern::escape for the root prefix only, retaining user include/exclude
syntax. Runnable tests verify actual analysis bytes and selected-input preservation
under a bracket-containing root. This is the same audited root-cause fix, not an
additional discovery policy or dependency. Existing standalone preparation remains
preserved and must not later be merged as duplicate work.


Windows CI at 9938173 exposed a skipped explicit failing script. Source review of
[glob 0.3.3](https://docs.rs/glob/0.3.3/src/glob/lib.rs.html) confirmed that escaping
the canonical Windows namespace changes its filesystem prefix. Normalize Disk/UNC
namespaces for glob transport only, keep filesystem prefixes literal, escape only
directory components and join patterns using native path operations. The captured
root is unchanged. Explicit include patterns with no files now fail instead of
reporting successful no-op execution. New native/canonical-root execution markers
run on every platform; network UNC execution remains unverified.

The same review found generated filenames could overwrite another selected script
or hook, DESCRIPTION or environment configuration. Before renderer invocation,
compare all concrete output/asset paths against the complete selected-input set
and reject authoritative project/environment metadata filenames. Fake-renderer
fixtures prove those failures happen before scripts, VERSION or ignore writes.
Amended exact-head CI and independent re-review remain required.


## Explicit directory ownership and local initialization

**Different (approved):** runtime directory resolution requires declared nonempty
paths and never invents missing labels or suffix subpaths. This supersedes earlier
in-memory directory-default behavior, including read-only path queries. Missing
configuration can still be queried as an empty inventory; builds require active
configuration. Storage content labels must exist, and relative storage locations
resolve against the captured root. Selected cleanup and project-render staging require `cache`; upload-only empty
analysis does not require an unused cache mapping.
Rendered documentation requires `docs`. Cache cleanup uses the declared mapping,
not a parallel hard-coded `_tmp` tree.

**Same preset / different timing:** pinned projr
`3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d`, `R/yml-dir.R:334–345`, supplies
`raw-data: _raw_data`, `cache: _tmp`, `output: _output`. Rust local-only
`proj --project . --non-interactive init directories` writes those explicit paths
once when no base/active profile exists. Existing configuration stays byte-for-byte
intact. No scripts field is generated: absence preserves discovery, while an
existing explicit empty list stays empty. No Git/GitHub/R setup is invoked.
The Rust accepted label-prefix subset still differs from projr's broader labels;
this slice does not claim full schema parity or R frontend changes.

Ponytail full-mode review reused the shared resolver and existing tempfile
dependency rather than adding a directory framework. Existing malformed/unreadable
config preservation tests remain; new tests cover missing paths, undeclared labels,
case collisions, explicit storage references, cache ownership, no-executable local
init, preserved base/legacy/profile bytes and actual default-discovered Python
output. Remote CI and independent review are pending. Init is not an atomic
transaction against filesystem failures or concurrent replacement.

Independent PR139 review removed an over-broad production cache prerequisite.
Only selected operations that consume cache require its mapping. Explicit empty

## Environment input validation (prepared)

**Same precedence / deliberate error handling difference:** inherited OS values
win over local, earlier environment profiles, then base assignments. Preserve
non-Unicode inherited values rather than treating them as absent. Reject empty,
equals-containing or NUL keys and NUL values before calling OS mutation APIs.
Read whole files with propagated errors rather than `lines().flatten()`; required
file errors and directory inputs cannot silently bypass validation or loop.
Diagnostics include paths/line numbers, never assignment values. Same-file
validation finishes before assignments from that file are applied. Ignore writes
in explicit activation occur only after validation succeeds.

Ponytail full-mode review traced all load/assignment callers and reused existing
configuration-entry presence checks. No parser dependency was added. Prepared CLI
checks cover invalid/NUL entries, directory and permission-denied required files,
secret-free diagnostics, actual inherited/local/profile/base child values and no
analysis invocation on errors. Remote checks/review are pending.

This bounded fix does **not** make EnvGuard thread-safe: process-global environment
mutation remains a known risk until per-run values and profiles reach all child
commands and Git/preflight consumers. No credential handling or CAS code changes.
## Prepared managed-state restoration invariant (not yet verified)

The restoration implementation under preparation replaces the legacy middle-only
catch and synthesized development-version rollback. Before controlled production
mutations, capture exact bytes, permissions and absence for VERSION, ignore files,
root configuration/state and existing root regular files; selected in-project
inputs; declared output/docs directory trees; and concrete individual renderer
output/asset paths. Capture initially absent parent directories too. Declared
external output/docs paths are supported. Raw data, Git internals, arbitrary
external user-script effects and cache contents are not backed up. Managed trees
containing symlinks or unsupported entries are rejected rather than followed.

Backups use existing tempfile and streaming std::fs copies in private OS temporary
recovery storage outside disposable project cache. No project mapping is invented,
and cache-free upload-only operations remain supported. Recovery sources are copied
to temporary restore staging before any current target is removed. Missing recovery
bytes leave intact current state alone and are reported as unavailable.

One local failure boundary covers ignore synchronization, cleanup, all pre/both/
post hooks, engine configuration, execution, output promotion and VERSION writing.
Promotion errors propagate; renderer configuration is restored byte-for-byte on
success and failure. VERSION changes only after hooks/render/promotion succeed.
Failures and caught panics restore captured state. All restore entries are attempted;
if restoration fails, retain recovery bytes and report both the original failure
and restoration failures with the backup path. Substituted links are rejected.

After local success, storage export/Git publication form a separate failure phase:
publication failure reports successful local analysis and retains the new local
release. Export precedes requested post-output cleanup so archives contain actual
build bytes. A failure during this later cleanup is explicitly reported as such;
there is no external publication rollback. No pre-build Git snapshot or second
post-build commit is needed. Upstream selection/native credentials and publication
retry identity remain separate unfinished work.

Prepared checks cover each hook/analysis failure, initially absent VERSION, exact
old output/docs bytes and empty directories, renderer execution/missing promotion,
exact YAML comments/render lists, restore-failure backup retention with external
sentinels, and successful local analysis followed by failed storage publication.
These are unrun: no local compilation under memory pressure; remote CI and
independent review are still required. No power-loss atomicity, concurrent-writer
or global script-side-effect guarantee is claimed. M2 attempt/release records and
analysis-free retry commands remain open.


PR141 review corrections: normalize selected-input identities before comparing
root containment (including Windows namespace forms); require nonempty supported
document artifacts before project promotion; remove prior expected individual
artifacts and project staging immediately before rendering. New regressions cover
nested scripts/hooks modifying or deleting themselves, empty renderer staging,
stale individual artifacts, cache purge during failed analysis, and unavailable
recovery bytes without further deletion. These amendments require fresh remote
CI and independent review. Project artifact scanning remains a conservative
supported-document check, not a complete renderer manifest guarantee.


Further review keeps project promotion conservative: require a freshly created
tree containing a nonempty supported document, rather than guessing per-input
filenames from incomplete document-only format metadata. Fake PDF rendering tests
cover explicit and inherited project formats. Complete expected-output manifests
remain unimplemented; individual document format inference is still a separate
known limitation. Selected managed script/hook paths reject symlinks along the
original path before canonical identity comparison. System recovery temp anchors
are canonicalized, including cache-free operations, without weakening user-path
symlink rejection.


Bookdown's framework-controlled `<book_filename>_files` source/destination are
resolved and guarded before writes, with default `_main` and portable custom stems.
Their exact prior bytes/presence join the recovery set. A fake successful render
followed by a failing post-hook checks both default/custom native asset trees and
released docs are restored. Unsupported path-like stems fail instead of traversing
outside the project. Remote verification and independent review remain required.


## Per-command build environment isolation

**Deliberate implementation change:** build_project resolves inherited OS values,
explicit profiles, local/earlier-profile/base environment files and required keys
without modifying std::env. The same immutable context drives YAML profile selection,
clear-output/installation/interaction controls, interpreter dependency probes,
scripts/hooks/renderers and existing Git capability/preflight/publication commands.
Child commands receive a captured environment, with the resolved project root and
intentional script profile values applied per command. Inherited non-Unicode values
remain intact. Existing Git credential selection/policy is forwarded, not redesigned.

Prepared remote checks force two library builds with different roots, profiles and
fixture values to overlap while an unrelated child observes the unchanged parent.
Mock R and Git commands verify probes and execution receive file-supplied values.
Existing input/preflight/preview/root-context tests remain. Ponytail full-mode review
reuses shared parsers and the standard Command.env_clear/envs API, with no global
mutex or new dependency. No credentials are formatted through Debug or diagnostics.
Remote CI and independent review are pending.

Legacy public EnvGuard activation/assignment APIs and CLI startup guards still
mutate process state and are explicitly not safe concurrent environment APIs.
The guarantee is bounded to the build path and commands receiving this context;
unrelated external code that concurrently mutates std::env remains outside it.
Native Git authentication/upstream policy and broader environment sanitization are
separate unfinished work. R package and CAS code are unchanged.


PR143 Windows review correction: inherited native keys/values are passed through,
but non-ASCII assignment/required keys in environment files are rejected early
with a precise diagnostic. This deliberately bounded support avoids approximating
Windows Unicode case identity and allowing a file alias to override an inherited
key. ASCII case precedence and native non-Unicode values retain their dedicated
platform tests. Unicode alias rejection is tested on Windows before analysis or
authoritative writes; complete Unicode assignment-key support is not claimed.

## Captured-root execution and explicit renderer layouts

**Different/new, approved root policy:** relative to pinned projr
`3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d` (`R/engine.R`, `R/path.R`) and the
audited Rust script-parent cwd, scripts/hooks now start in the captured root.
Shallow default enumeration and explicitly selected nested paths are preserved.
Quarto uses its supported `--execute-dir`; individual R Markdown supplies
`knit_root_dir`. R Markdown filenames are trailing data arguments to fixed R code,
avoiding apostrophe/source interpolation. See [Rscript arguments](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/Rscript.html),
[rmarkdown render](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/docs/reference/render.html), and
[Quarto render controls](https://quarto.org/docs/cli/render.html).

**Different/new, conservative supported subset:** native R Markdown `output` and
Quarto `format` select one known format; PDF/Word no longer guess HTML. Unknown or
multiple formats, individual inherited metadata/unsupported output layouts,
document-rendering hooks and nested Quarto roots fail early. This deliberately
rejects previously guessed/unsafe layouts rather than claiming full renderer support.
`clear_output` and ignore choices are finite early-validated values. No R production
code changes, direct IDE verification or automatic preview isolation are included.

Ponytail full-mode review traced execution/preflight/promotion callers and reused
existing YAML, command/environment and path safety facilities without new dependencies.
Remote regressions are prepared for real nested Python hook/script ordering and cwd,
safe R argument transport, HTML/PDF/Word promotion, nested roots, invalid controls and
unsupported layouts preserving config/VERSION. CI and independent review are pending.

## CAS integrity hardening (existing issues 688–690)

**Different/new:** the audited Rust baseline scanned/hash-named files, reopened them
for copy, trusted existing objects, normalized Unix literal backslashes into slashes,
accepted missing/file sources as empty snapshots and treated manifest existence as
verification. This slice rejects missing/non-directory sources and unsafe overlap,
linked/unsupported entries, ambiguous logical paths and malformed/non-ASCII digests
before unsafe lookup. Literal backslash names are rejected rather than conflated
with nested paths. Original source bytes are read only.

Hash the exact stream copied into temporary storage; validate existing object bytes
before trusting the digest key. Immutable objects/manifests publish without clobber;
manifest conflicts fail instead of truncating existing bytes. Manifest inspection
parses/validates JSON and filename hash; file inspection hashes referenced objects.
Index replacement uses complete staged bytes with CSV escaping for label/version.
Temp fixtures use canonical physical paths so macOS system temp aliases do not
silently weaken user-controlled symlink checks.

Ponytail full-mode review reuses BLAKE3, tempfile, shared path guards and standard
streaming I/O. No new dependency or CAS schema/version-identity redesign. Prepared
remote checks cover malformed paths/digests, Unix backslash collisions, missing/file
sources, corrupt existing objects, changed source paths during stream copy, injected
read errors, immutable manifest conflict and index failure with old state preserved,
CSV metadata escaping and actual referenced-object hashes. Existing empty-directory
and dedup/version-sensitive manifest tests remain. Remote CI/review are pending.

This advances existing MiguelRodo/issues#688–690 rather than creating duplicate
roadmap issues. Broader CAS lifecycle/GC, a consistent concurrent-source snapshot,
multi-writer index updates and crash durability remain open. Failed index publication
may leave a complete unindexed manifest; object residue is valid but not a successful
indexed export. There is no full cross-filesystem metadata transaction or global
scientific reproducibility guarantee. Existing R package remains untouched.


PR145 review adds shared manifest file/directory prefix-collision validation.
Logical files `a` and `a/b` cannot coexist, independent of input order or intervening
names. Both inspection strategies are tested with real digest-matching objects so
the rejection proves layout validation, not an unrelated missing-object failure.

CAS metadata readers/writers require regular files before reading existing manifest
or index bytes; Unix named-pipe regressions use a bounded completion check so hostile
special metadata cannot block verification or ingestion indefinitely.

## Optional Git publication and transient credential safety

**Different/new (approved explicit-action policy):** no commit/fetch/push/token
requirement is inferred from Git metadata. Omitted commits and not_behind checks
are off; explicit actions use the per-run environment. Commit builds fail before
writes when Git already contains changes, preserving unrelated work; staged-index
no-op is success. Publish one HEAD refspec to the configured current upstream,
never origin/main. Custom pushRemote/pushDefault/remote.push routing is conservatively
rejected early rather than silently choosing the wrong destination. Local release
success remains distinct from publication failure. The retained reference projr and
legacy Rust are evidence, not authority for these newer confirmed decisions.

Native Git authentication is default. Explicit use_proj_cred_helper enables only
existing single-line environment tokens on standard HTTPS github.com remotes;
no build calls GitHub CLI token discovery. Fixed helper code accepts only HTTPS
github.com credential requests; the token is quoted environment data, not argv or
shell source. The helper list resets for that one command; no persistent config or
credentials are created. Captured network failures report status without reflecting
potential secret stderr. Other hosts use native configured authentication.
See Git's [credential helper protocol](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitcredentials)
and [upstream/refspec documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push).

Ponytail full-mode review reuses native Git, existing providers and shared environment
context. No new dependency or credential store. Prepared remote checks use fake
Git/GH to cover zero implicit calls, configured fetch only, real upstream/refspec,
no-op/single commit, dirty-input preservation, native versus opt-in helper behavior,
host/protocol denial, punctuation as literal token data, helper reset and secret-free
argv/diagnostics. No real network/auth action is tested. Remote CI and independent
review are pending; CAS integrity and analysis-free publication retries remain open.

PR143 reviewer note: the shared Windows ASCII assignment restriction also applies
to public legacy EnvGuard::track_and_set, not just file-based keys. Inherited native
environment values remain preserved; the legacy mutation APIs remain outside the
build-path concurrency guarantee.


PR144 review guards force untracked-file and submodule visibility during the clean
check, reject pushurl and multiple effective push URLs before writes, and disable
follow-tags/submodule recursion for the single explicit push. Extra destinations
are also checked at dispatch. Git's executable is resolved explicitly from the
per-run PATH (git.exe on Windows), avoiding native parent-PATH fallback in both
availability checks and execution. Remote fixtures cover hidden untracked content,
fan-out/redirection rejection and explicit suppression flags. Fresh exact-head
checks and independent re-review are required.

The same preflight also rejects mirror pushes, absent remotes, multiple tracking
merge entries and effective push/fetch endpoint differences (including expanded
pushInsteadOf). Destination inspection uses get-url --push --all before controlled
build writes. Native Git configuration is read only; no remote/auth settings are
rewritten. Fake regressions assert each unsupported case preserves VERSION and
unrelated private bytes and never reaches add/commit/fetch/push.


Captured push identity includes checked-out branch, upstream remote/ref and expanded
effective endpoint, without Debug exposure. Revalidate the complete supported
identity immediately before commit and again before push. Hook/script changes to
URL, pushurl, mirror, branch, ref or remote fail publication without redirecting the
push; successful local VERSION/output are retained. Fake regressions switch those
values after an analysis marker and assert no add/commit/push occurs. This guards
within-run mutation, not an atomic lock against concurrent external Git changes.


The sibling public post_build_sync API now uses the same captured-context checked
publication helper as build_project. A fake commit hook changing the endpoint is
rejected before push. Explicit Git lookup anchors directories absolutely but preserves
the candidate leaf spelling, supporting symlink-based name dispatchers; a fake
git-to-dispatcher symlink regression prevents argv[0] canonicalization regressions.

## Preview preservation despite managed-state writes

**Different/new:** the cooperating-script-only PR123 preview guarantee is extended
using reviewed exact-byte recovery from PR141. Captured release output/docs,
VERSION/config/root files, selected scripts/hooks, local publication stores and
ordinary VCS metadata restore after successful and failing previews. The pinned
projr `3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d` remains workflow evidence, not a
tested runtime parity claim. No R changes or publication calls are introduced.

**Bounded:** cache artifacts remain; arbitrary undeclared/external script effects,
worktree VCS pointer targets, concurrent writes/power loss and automatic redirection
of every script output are not covered. Recovery rejects unsafe overlaps/links,
preserves original missing/present state and never deletes a current target before
its existing recovery bytes are prepared. Restore failure is a failed preview,
even when analysis returned zero, and retains available private recovery bytes.

Ponytail full-mode review reused BuildState, filesystem identity/overlap guards and
existing command environments without a new transaction framework/dependency.
Prepared remote regressions deliberately delete/alter captured outputs, archive,
config, selected nested source and VCS state on success/failure, including pre/post
hooks with explicit empty analysis. Cache result bytes survive; no framework Git or
export calls occur. A missing-backup success path verifies honest failure and safe
current-state preservation. CI/independent review pending.

PR148 review uses one resolved cache identity for both private-storage and managed
target overlap checks. Dot-dot cache spellings with ancestor/descendant or shared
absent-parent publication paths reject before analysis; a disjoint existing-parent
case preserves actual cache artifact bytes. Recovery must not remove allowed cache.

Recovery overlap comparisons conservatively fold ASCII names on all platforms,
including absent suffixes (Windows/default macOS can alias them). Missing Unicode
components reject only when overlap comparison reaches an ambiguous alias; disjoint
existing/ASCII directory prefixes rule out overlap before a Unicode output leaf. Actual
filesystem paths retain original spelling; these identities only bound overlap and
deduplication. Cross-platform absent-case-alias fixtures fail before cache writes.

mismatched inputs; help smoke failures are no longer swallowed. CI/review pending.

## M1 machine transport (issue682, existing error work87)

**New:** protocol-v1 opt-in JSON envelope and capability version, with static
structured failure codes/nonzero exits. Existing human CLI remains default.
Queries use explicit-root typed APIs rather than stripping progress prose; config
validation returns no raw parameter values. Other command families reuse the
existing CLI/domain paths in a noninteractive worker, redirecting child stdout
and stderr directly to stderr without log buffering. No credentials/config/argv
are copied into protocol errors. User/third-party logs are not auto-redacted.

Pinned projr `3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d` is the workflow reference;
this machine transport is a new language-neutral boundary, not established R API
compatibility. No R code changes, finer domain-error taxonomy, release record or
publication-retry semantics. Existing anyhow handling remains the domain layer;
issue87 is not duplicated by a cross-module error rewrite.

Ponytail full-mode review uses existing clap/serde/anyhow/query/CLI facilities,
standard subprocess stream redirection and no new dependencies. Prepared remote
tests cover capability negotiation, typed queries without prose/secrets, malformed
config/arguments/root, missing interpreter, child failure/logs, local init and
version mutation. CI/independent review pending. Managed preview output isolation
remains outstanding and is advertised as false, not described as sandboxing.

## Explicit safe/final resource lookup and fragments

- **Same/intended:** projr90be501 R/dir-get.R48–86,229–244,284–301 routes safe
  output/data/docs into first cache-class/version context. Rust preserves merged

  CLI default until production promotion consumes safe outputs. This avoids changing

  renderer contexts/staging, default switch and native cwd follow separately.
- **Tests prepared for remote CI:** declaration order opposed to alphabetical order,
  dev/release cache keys, data/docs/exact labels, absolute external mappings,

Invalid/stale inherited run-context files deliberately fail closed, including an
explicit other-project query when the snapshot cannot first be validated. A valid
snapshot is discarded for a different explicit root. This is a documented current
boundary, not a promise that explicit selection repairs a corrupt descriptor.

Shared output/data/docs classification now governs logical lookup, managed capture

ordinary-absolute-cache regression with two roles targeting result.txt and preserved

## Cache-backed consumers and output lifecycle

- **Same intended routing:** pinned projr90be501 R/dir-get.R68–84,247–253 and
  R/version.R433–438 route safe generated output through cache/projr/v<version>.
  Rust consumers now use the captured active version/selected cache rather than
  old VERSION text/literal cache. Fresh render artifacts are retained in versioned
  docs cache; final destinations remain separately configured.
- **Same broad ordering, tightened by user:** start hooks, other preparation,
  pre-clear immediately before analysis, post-clear immediately after successful
  analysis, promotion/finalization, end hooks immediately before next-dev bump.
  R's production clear_output=NULL falls back env then pre; development defaults
  never. R has no general runtime options/settings YAML section and does not read
  build.clear_output. Rust's settings.output-clear-stage default none and YAML over
  environment are deliberate approved differences; legacy never remains compatible.
- **Different/fixed:** final clearing never deletes preview outputs; renderer cache
  targets use active v-prefixed version. No old-cache sweep is performed implicitly.
  Production old_dev_remove:true is rejected rather than silently ignored.
- **Boundaries:** path lookup defaults still final/absolute in this intermediate
  consumer slice. R-data naming/normalization, default switching and embedding
  fallback remain separately pending. Cache-free operations remain supported.
  Fresh renderer-tree validation is conservative, not a complete manifest; cached
  analysis residue from retries has no M2 attempt/provenance guarantee.
- **Publication:** external storage/Git happen after a successful local release;
  later publication/end-hook failure preserves it and is reported distinctly.
  No remote rollback or all-files sandbox guarantee is claimed.
- **Tests prepared:** real Python success/failure/preview clear-event fixtures,
  exact version/order/cache/final-byte assertions, YAML/environment/CLI precedence,
  and invalid-layer rejection. Remote pinned-image checks are pending; actual
  real-render embedding acceptance follows, not inferred from fake renderers.
- **Ponytail full self-review:** reused per-command context, shared destination guards,
  temporary directories and existing guarded recursive copy. No new dependencies,
  process cwd mutation, generalized transaction framework or R package edits.
